sentence: This project works out the mathematics behind how thin boundary layers, turbulence and large waves behave in fluids.
This project builds a low-cost kit that uses computer vision to observe and track honey bees in natural settings.
This project tries to find out whether electricity and mechanical forces can turn stem cells from fat tissue into cartilage cells called chondrocytes.
This project studies how to control and stabilize quantum systems that are not in equilibrium, using periodic driving from lasers.
This project develops a way for autonomous surface vehicles to map water quality and to separate sensor uncertainty from model uncertainty.
This project studies how CRISPR nucleases work and uses them to build a biosensor that detects DNA differences linked to disease.
This project builds learning activities that show how attacks can weaken deep learning models and how to defend against them.
This project develops mathematical tools to understand the long-term dynamics and rigidity of groups that model negatively curved-space symmetries.
This project tests a laser-driven particle accelerator that uses plasma to reach extremely high energies over much shorter distances.
This project studies how plastic polymer chains interact with catalyst surfaces during chemical recycling.
This project brings together researchers to share recent results in commutative algebra, the study of polynomial equations.
This project uses ultracold atoms held in laser beams to study quantum spin liquids and other exotic quantum phases of matter.
This project studies how quarks and gluons behave when atomic nuclei collide at nearly the speed of light.
This project builds computer tools that predict what plant enzymes do and lab tools that test those predictions.
This project links on-ground and remotely sensed data with models to study how crop production and water resources respond to climate change.
